objective: Give a project one development line where every program's landed work meets, composed and checked by a single line owner the control plane starts when there is work and stops when the line has caught up; and let a program have at most one live run at a time. Pipkin M1b, PK-3 (PIP-9). The authority is the plan document stored with this contract.

successCriteria.outcome: Starting a run of a program that already has a live run is refused, atomically in the control plane, naming the live run; a run still pending with no attach and no dispatch after a short grace period is ended as interrupted (never started) and no longer counts.

A project opts in with a line branch in nightshift.config.json; when a remote run's program branch is pushed to GitHub, the control plane queues its new range for the line and, if no line owner is live, starts exactly one.

The line owner takes everything queued (up to a cap), merges main and then each program branch's new range onto the line head, runs the landing checks on the result, and publishes the line with a compare-and-swap push; a failed batch is composed one range at a time; the queue and the owner survive the machine dying, and two owners never run at once.

When a composition conflicts or its checks go red, a resolver agent repairs it from the line head on the line owner's machine; its fix lands on the line after the same checks and an examination by a different model, and is recorded as a decision; after three failed attempts or an hour the composition is parked and reported, and the rest of the queue goes on.
Work the control plane starts by itself is held to a per-project monthly compute cap (default $25); at the cap the line stops composing and says why, and programs keep landing on their branches.

`nightshift line status` shows the line's head, what is queued, what each composed commit contains (program ranges, its verification, any resolver decision), and any parked composition; and the architecture records the project line.

constraints: Runs land on their program branches exactly as today; a run never waits on the line, and nothing the line does can fail a run.
Programs still reach main through their own pull requests; nothing in this program merges or pushes to main.
The line moves only by the publisher's compare-and-swap push, and only one line owner per line is ever live.
A project without a line configured behaves exactly as today.
No new credential reaches a run's engine: the line owner reads GitHub as a machine already does, and only the publisher writes.
A verification made on the line is never landing evidence for a run.
Windows keeps working: nothing added assumes a POSIX shell or path.

decisions.question: Who composes onto the project line: each run for itself, or one line owner?
options: One line owner per line, started by the control plane when work is queued and stopped when idle
Each run composes its own strands, with compare-and-swap pushes
decisions.leaning: One line owner per line, started by the control plane when work is queued and stopped when idle
decisions.answer: One line owner per line, started by the control plane when work is queued and stopped when idle
decisions.rationale: It removes the engine's need for GitHub mid-run and for push outcomes, outlives any one run, and is the one place batching and later bisection can live (PK-7).

decisions.question: When and in what units does the line owner compose?
options: Natural batching: compose at once when idle, and take everything that arrived meanwhile as one batch, by program-branch range; a failed batch is composed one range at a time
Each strand on its own as it lands
Collect landings for a fixed time window
decisions.leaning: Natural batching: compose at once when idle, and take everything that arrived meanwhile as one batch, by program-branch range; a failed batch is composed one range at a time
decisions.answer: Natural batching: compose at once when idle, and take everything that arrived meanwhile as one batch, by program-branch range; a failed batch is composed one range at a time
decisions.rationale: No added latency at low volume, batches grow with load, a program's own strands are already proven together, and the fallback is the simple form of the bisection PK-7 brings.

decisions.question: May the resolver land its own fix onto the line?
options: Yes, after the landing checks and an examination by a different model, recorded as a decision for later review
No, it stops for the owner
Mechanical conflicts only; red checks wait for the owner
decisions.leaning: Yes, after the landing checks and an examination by a different model, recorded as a decision for later review
decisions.answer: Yes, after the landing checks and an examination by a different model, recorded as a decision for later review
decisions.rationale: Runs fix and record rather than stop; nothing ships from the line in M1b, so a wrong fix costs a later repair.

decisions.question: How is work the control plane starts by itself bounded?
options: A per-project monthly compute cap (default $25), an hour per composition and three resolver attempts, under the org's ceilings
decisions.leaning: A per-project monthly compute cap (default $25), an hour per composition and three resolver attempts, under the org's ceilings
decisions.answer: A per-project monthly compute cap (default $25), an hour per composition and three resolver attempts, under the org's ceilings
decisions.rationale: The first work that spends without the owner starting it; models run on the org's subscriptions, so the attempt and time limits bound quota and the cap bounds machine spend.

decisions.question: How does main relate to the line in M1b?
options: Programs still reach main through their own pull requests, merged with a merge commit; the line takes main in before composing; a conflict the resolver fixed on the line is fixed again at the pull request, with the line's fix as reference
A pull request from the line to main
decisions.leaning: Programs still reach main through their own pull requests, merged with a merge commit; the line takes main in before composing; a conflict the resolver fixed on the line is fixed again at the pull request, with the line's fix as reference
decisions.answer: Programs still reach main through their own pull requests, merged with a merge commit; the line takes main in before composing; a conflict the resolver fixed on the line is fixed again at the pull request, with the line's fix as reference
decisions.rationale: main only ever receives whole programs; a line pull request would carry half-finished programs. M2's candidates feed main from the line and close the gap.

decisions.question: Does a local run's work reach the line?
options: Not in M1b: the line composes what reaches GitHub through the publisher, which is remote runs' program branches
Yes: local runs push their program branch with the owner's credentials and queue it
decisions.leaning: Not in M1b: the line composes what reaches GitHub through the publisher, which is remote runs' program branches
decisions.answer: Not in M1b: the line composes what reaches GitHub through the publisher, which is remote runs' program branches
decisions.rationale: The line composes what reaches GitHub through the publisher; a laptop pushing the line would be a new path trusting the owner's own credentials.

decisions.question: How does a run that never started stop counting as live?
options: The next start of that program ends a run still pending with no attach and no dispatch after a grace period as interrupted (never started)
A periodic sweep in the control plane
decisions.leaning: The next start of that program ends a run still pending with no attach and no dispatch after a grace period as interrupted (never started)
decisions.answer: The next start of that program ends a run still pending with no attach and no dispatch after a grace period as interrupted (never started)
decisions.rationale: The next start can settle it; a sweeper is more moving parts for the same case.

decisions.question: What is the line setting called, and its default branch?
options: `"line": { "branch": "nightshift/develop" }` in nightshift.config.json, absent meaning off; docs say "project line" to keep it apart from the provisional line
decisions.leaning: `"line": { "branch": "nightshift/develop" }` in nightshift.config.json, absent meaning off; docs say "project line" to keep it apart from the provisional line
decisions.answer: `"line": { "branch": "nightshift/develop" }` in nightshift.config.json, absent meaning off; docs say "project line" to keep it apart from the provisional line
decisions.rationale: Opt-in and explicit, and the docs keep it apart from the provisional line.
